title: Late routing congestion at top-level pin field after CTS
design_context: 7nm, 1.2M placeable instances, 87 macros (mostly SRAM), 2 clocks: 800MHz core and 400MHz IO, commercial P&R
prior_state: Utilization 77%, GRC overflow 2.3%, peak bin overflow 12%, 0 DRC at placement, post-CTS WNS -45ps, TNS -0.8ns
observation: Detailed routing stalled at 93% with 1840 opens/shorts, 88% of overflow concentrated in 400um x 400um channel between two macro rows, pin density 620 pins per 100um on M2/M3. severity: HIGH
hypothesis: High pin density from two mirrored SRAM banks facing each other created M2 pin-access conflict compounded by M2/M3 power strap alignment blocking track access, not global routing resource shortage.

candidates_considered.action: Increase die area 3% to drop utilization to 72%
candidates_considered.rejected_because: Requires top-level floorplan re-signoff and bump map invalidation, 2-week schedule hit, impacts all blocks.

candidates_considered.action: Flip every other SRAM macro 180deg to stagger pins
candidates_considered.rejected_because: Risk of timing regression on 87 macros, requires full CTS rerun, estimated IR increase +8mV on flipped orientation.

candidates_considered.action: Lower utilization 5% via placement blockage in channel
candidates_considered.rejected_because: Pushes cells into already congested periphery, adds 5% area penalty and does not solve pin-access root cause.

candidates_considered.action: Apply non-default routing rule widening M2 pitch in channel
candidates_considered.rejected_because: Widening pitch reduces available tracks further and worsens pin access, increases overflow to 3.1% in trial run.

chosen_intervention: Kept floorplan, added 2.5um placement halo around macro pins in channel, swapped 14% of high-pin-density cells in hotspot from 9T to 10.5T variants with double-row pin access, created routing guide blocking 50% of M2/M3 in first 2um above macro pins forcing escape to M4, reran detailed route honoring halo.
post_state: GRC overflow 0.18%, peak overflow 2.1%, detailed route 100% complete with 42 DRCs fixed in second pass, effective utilization 76.5%, WNS -78ps, TNS -1.1ns
expert_assessment: Right call for schedule - pin-access spreading plus selective M2/M3 blockage addresses root cause without top-level churn. Lesson: distinguish global vs pin-access congestion by overflow clustering and pin density. Would not transfer if hotspot were due to power-mesh blockage or high-fanout global nets.
weakest_point: The 2.5um halo value is an estimate that must be tuned to the specific library pin-access width and should be verified with pin-access checker.

title: Input-delay overconstraint masquerading as logic depth failure
design_context: 28nm, 650k placeable instances, 12 macros, 1 clock 500MHz (2ns period), commercial synthesis and P&R
prior_state: Utilization 68%, GRC overflow 0.4%, WNS -420ps, TNS -18.3ns, 12400 failing endpoints at post-route STA, no DRCs
observation: Slack histogram shows 11800 endpoints failing -10ps to -80ps, all startpoints from 3 input ports data_bus[31:0], all endpoints within 2 logic levels of input flops, 92% share same clock uncertainty and same input delay group, worst path -420ps outlier from one input with large delay. severity: MODERATE
hypothesis: Failures are due to unrealistic input delay budget 0.7*clock applied to slow board trace, not insufficient cell drive or placement distance; shape of many small failures sharing same input indicates constraint problem.

candidates_considered.action: Upsize drivers on failing paths and add useful skew
candidates_considered.rejected_because: Would add 12% area and 18mW leakage for no benefit since root is input arrival, and increases IR drop in dense input cluster.

candidates_considered.action: Re-place input flops closer to pads
candidates_considered.rejected_because: Requires IO movement risking DRC, 3-day schedule cost, does not fix 0.7*clock input delay which remains unrealistic.
Changes latency visible to system, requires RTL change and re-verification, not allowed in ECO window.

chosen_intervention: Audited SDC, input delay was 1.4ns derived from early board estimate. Corrected to measured 0.65ns per IO spec, updated set_input_delay for data_bus group to 0.65ns max / 0.15ns min, added set_input_transition 120ps, re-ran STA without netlist change.
post_state: WNS -28ps, TNS -0.12ns, 180 failing endpoints remaining (true logic paths), utilization unchanged, no area change
expert_assessment: Correct triage - signature of many small shared-startpoint failures is classic constraint issue. General lesson: check slack distribution and startpoint commonality before physical fix. Would not transfer if failures were spread across logic cones with large negative slack and no common startpoint.
weakest_point: The corrected 0.65ns input delay value is plausible but would need board-level SI validation from IO timing spec.

title: Cross-block output budget allocation between encryption core and fabric
design_context: 7nm, block A 1.1M instances 48 macros, block B 0.9M instances 22 macros, interface 256-bit data at 1GHz (1ns), commercial P&R and STA
prior_state: Top-level budget 1ns, initially 50/50 split: 0.5ns for block A clock-to-out and 0.5ns for block B in-to-reg. Block A WNS -110ps, TNS -1.2ns, Block B WNS +180ps.
observation: Block A output paths failing 80-110ps, all share last 3 stages of ECC logic, Block B has 180ps positive slack on same interface. severity: MODERATE
hypothesis: 50/50 split over-constrains block A which contains deeper logic before output; budget should be weighted by logic depth 60/40 to avoid unnecessary upsizing in A while leaving margin for B routing.

candidates_considered.action: Keep 50/50 and upsize Block A output logic
candidates_considered.rejected_because: Costs 4% area in A and +22mW dynamic power for marginal benefit, creates IR hotspot near output pins.

candidates_considered.action: Move to 40/60 giving more to B (0.4ns A, 0.6ns B)
candidates_considered.rejected_because: Makes A WNS worse to -210ps requiring floorplan change, no benefit as B already has slack.

candidates_considered.action: Add false path between blocks and rely on top-level closure
candidates_considered.rejected_because: Hides real timing, risk of silicon failure at 1GHz, violates methodology and would be caught in top-level STA.

chosen_intervention: Derived budget from logic depth: counted avg 14 FO4 stages in A after last flop vs 6 in B before first flop, allocated 0.62ns to A and 0.38ns to B, encoded as set_output_delay 0.38ns on A and set_input_delay 0.62ns on B with 40ps uncertainty margin, documented in SDC header.
post_state: Block A WNS +15ps, TNS +0.02ns, Block B WNS +55ps, top-level combined interface slack +22ps, no area change
expert_assessment: Right trade - budgets should follow logic depth not arbitrary 50/50. Lesson: measure depth and document alternative splits. 50/50 is safe default but wastes power when asymmetry is large. Would not transfer if interface had CDC or multicycle intent requiring different exception handling.
weakest_point: The 14 vs 6 FO4 depth split is illustrative and would need extraction from real STA path-length report in practice.

claim: All major browsers still require secure context + COOP same-origin + COEP require-corp or credentialless for SharedArrayBuffer and Wasm threads; postMessage throws for SAB unless crossOriginIsolated true
notes: Verified from MDN: To use shared memory your document must be in a secure context and cross-origin isolated. When cross-origin isolated postMessage no longer throws for SAB.

claim: Requirement unchanged in 2026: COOP same-origin + COEP require-corp or credentialless needed for cross-origin isolation; Permissions-Policy cross-origin-isolated must not block; no spec change found for 2026
notes: MDN COOP page states certain features such as SharedArrayBuffer only available if document is cross-origin isolated, need COOP same-origin and COEP require-corp credentialless. No 2026 change document found, claim UNVERIFIED for change.

claim: WebGPU stable in Chrome/Edge 113+ (May 2023), Safari 26+ Sep 2025 macOS Tahoe/iOS, Firefox Windows 141+ Jul 2025, Firefox macOS Apple Silicon 145+ Oct 2025, other platforms behind flag expecting 2026 GA. Compute shaders are core to WebGPU, availability follows WebGPU support.

notes: Chrome blog says WebGPU spec makes timestamp queries optional due to timing attack concerns, quantizing to 100 microseconds. MDN writeTimestamp also says timestamp-query feature must be enabled.

notes: web.dev article lists browser support: Chrome-based: Threads, SIMD, exception handling supported; Firefox Thread and SIMD supported; Safari Threads supported.

notes: Article states Wasm 3.0 standardized nine features including WasmGC, exception handling, tail calls, 64-bit memory, 128-bit SIMD.

claim: JSPI (WebAssembly.Suspending / promising) enabled by default in Chrome 137+, Firefox 153+, Node 25+, Safari TP 238+ as of May 2026. Firefox 139-152 flagged.
notes: PR description says JSPI enabled by default in Chrome 137+, Firefox 153+, Node 25+ (24 behind flag); Safari support landed in TP 238.

claim: webgpu Permissions-Policy defaults to self, blocking cross-origin and sandboxed iframes from navigator.gpu. Requires parent iframe allow=webgpu and Permissions-Policy header webgpu=* to delegate.
notes: Commit message explains webgpu policy defaults to self, blocks game iframes, fix via allow=webgpu and webgpu=* header.

claim: Cross-origin iframe cannot achieve crossOriginIsolated for SAB unless both top and iframe serve COOP/COEP and parent allows; many implementations fall back to top-level page instead of iframe because GitHub Pages cannot set headers. So wallet embedding requiring isolation+WebGPU is blocked in iframe by default.
notes: Inferred from multiple issues: demo uses multithreading so must be cross-origin isolated, launches as own page rather than iframe. Verified weaker source, not authoritative spec.

claim: UNVERIFIED - no published 2026 measurements with reproducible harness found in authoritative docs. Only vendor repos claim client-side proving in browser using WebGPU with real-time benchmark UI but no methodology published.
notes: Repo mentions client-side proving in browser using WebGPU and real-time benchmarks but does not provide measured numbers, hardware, or harness. No 2026 paper found. Cell remains to be measured, not researched.
